name: Pragma Systems Field Polo
description:
A three-button short-sleeve polo in Pragma Systems' corporate grey-blue, with the company's geometric hexagon mark embroidered in white on the left chest. Cut in a relaxed fit to accommodate a range of body types and augmentation profiles — the shoulder and upper arm seams are double-reinforced with a gusseted construction that gives room without looking sloppy. The fabric is a durable synthetic piqué that holds its color through industrial washing and resists minor chemical splash.

Distributed to Pragma field technicians, infrastructure maintenance crews, and on-site support staff. Wearing one in the field means you're Pragma — or you want people to think you are. The polo is unremarkable in every intentional way: visible enough to identify you as staff, anonymous enough that nobody looks twice. Thousands of them exist across the city. Counterfeits are trivially easy to produce, which is both a problem and, for certain people, a useful feature.
what_it_says: I work for Pragma. Or I need you to think I do.
manufacturer: Pragma Systems (internal supply / Daltex Uniform Manufacturing)
story_hooks: A character acquires a Pragma polo and uses it to access a restricted infrastructure node — the shirt gets them through two checkpoints before someone notices the embroidery thread color is slightly wrong.
A Pragma field tech is found dead in a the Gray Zone district, still in uniform — his crew ID is missing but the shirt is intact.
Someone is selling counterfeit Pragma polos in the Gray Zone for Φ8 each — the buyer pool is more interesting than the seller realizes.

physical_description.visual_profile: A clean, utilitarian short-sleeve polo with subtle corporate authority. The silhouette reads as approachable but official—relaxed enough for fieldwork, structured enough to signal institutional affiliation. The Pragma geometric hexagon emblem on the left chest anchors the design without dominating it.
physical_description.fit: Relaxed through the torso with intentional gusseting at the shoulders and upper arms to accommodate augmented limbs and subdermal tech without looking oversized. Not form-fitting, but not baggy—designed for functionality across variable body types and enhancement profiles.
physical_description.primary_material: Durable synthetic piqué blend—machine-washable, chemical-resistant, holds dye through repeated industrial laundering. Lightweight enough for indoor climate-controlled environments, sturdy enough for warehouse and field deployment.
physical_description.texture: Smooth piqué weave with subtle texture; no loose threads or soft hand. Fabric has a slight sheen that catches light but reads as professional rather than reflective. Resists pilling and minor abrasion.
physical_description.color_scheme: Pragma Systems corporate grey-blue (a cool mid-tone that photographs as neutral under fluorescent and LED lighting). White embroidered hexagon on left chest. No accent stitching or trim.
physical_description.closures: Three-button front placket in white or grey polymer; functional rather than decorative. Buttons are set to take wear without stripping.
distinctive_features: Double-reinforced shoulder and upper arm seams with gusseted construction for augmentation clearance
White embroidered Pragma Systems hexagon geometric mark on left chest
Internally tagged with serialization (visible only when removed)
Subtle reflective thread in seams for low-light visibility (industrial standard)
Cut allows for subcutaneous augmentation profiles without fabric bunching
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 2–3 boundary: issued to corporate field staff, but the garment itself is mass-produced and functionally indistinguishable from working-class uniforms. Signals employment more than wealth.
physical_description.cultural_context: Wearing this marks you as Pragma Systems infrastructure support—technicians, maintenance crews, on-site logistics. It's a uniform of institutional affiliation, not rank. In the GLMZ, a genuine Pragma polo gets you past certain checkpoints; a counterfeit gets you detained or worse.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine when new, broken-in after a few weeks of fieldwork. Typical wear includes minor chemical staining, small pulls in the fabric from equipment contact, and fading in high-friction zones (collar, sleeve cuffs). Counterfeits often show sloppy embroidery and dye inconsistency.
